SGP Calculations with Pearson/PARCC/New Meridian
 History of SGP Calculations
 In general, because SGPs are norm referenced, they are scale
 agnostic only requiring students to take the same test at the
 same time.
 Given changing consortium state membership together with
 different test/form types, there are questions regarding the
 comparability of SGPs both within and across years.
 Issues related to mode of administration effect (within year,
 different groups) have been investigated by PARCC previously.
 Issues related to across year differences in growth due to
 changes in consortium membership or test form change (e.g.,
 2019 short-form use) have not been investigated.
 For 2019 spring analyses, NM, IL, NJ, BIE utilized an
 abbreviated form of the PARCC test. DC, MD, DoDEA utilized
 the flagship (long) form. NJ also post-equated its ELA test.
 We investigated whether changing state membership as well as
 test form differences led to appreciable differences in SGP
 results.

SGP Properties
 SGP Properties
 SGPs are uniformly distributed and uncorrelated with prior
 achievement at the individual level.
 State and consortium level SGPs (i.e., growth norms) are
 calculated.
 For large groups, entire states (state norms), or the consortium,
 mean(SGP ) ≈ 50.
 “Large” deviations from 50 or between groups usually indicates
 something is going on and worth investigating further.
 A state’s recent transition to different assessments at the high

Investigation of mean SGP differences
 Two approaches
 Probabilistic Difference
 Given sufficient historical data, mean SGPs can
 be investigated relative to the distribution of
 previous observations.
 A t-distribution or similar sample distribution can
 be used to formally calculate a p-values.
 In general, too few observations (3 years of mean
 SGPs for these analyses) were available for
 significance testing.
 Also, statistical significance doesn’t imply
 practical significance.
 Practical Difference
 Cohen’s D can be easily calculated for groups
 using SGPs.
 Because SGPs are uniform, the pooled within
 group standard deviation that forms the
 denominator is approximately 28.8 for most
 groups investigated.
 A mean(SGP ) difference of 5 (which is often
 used as a rule of thumb for practical differences)
 corresponds to a Cohen’s D of 0.17.

Investigation of mean SGP differences
 Results
 Historical consortium SGP results were recalculated using 2019
 state membership to examine year-to-year variation.
 Year-to-year differences uniformly negligible using 5 as the
 practical significance threshold.
 For state continuing with dual mode administration, mode
 effects continue to be detected.
